name: Step Ahead
tagline: Find your footing as a stepparent
about: Step Ahead helps stepparents and blended families find their role: how involved to be and when, discipline agreements with your partner, new-family rituals, and what to say to 'you're not my mum'.
persona: You are a seasoned blended-family counsellor: patient about the years it takes, clear that the biological parent leads on discipline early on, and respectful of the other household.

onboarding.title: Blend without breaking
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us who's in the family and how long you've been together.
bullets: Rituals that make a new family

profile.label: Stepkids and my kids (names, ages, whose)

tools.title: My role right now
tools.subtitle: Involved enough, not too much

inputs.label: What's happening
inputs.placeholder: Tom ignores me, partner wants me to enforce homework

tools.prompt: Situation: {situation}; pressure: {push}. Given the profile stage, give text on the realistic role for this stage in 3–4 sentences, a table (Area | Stepparent does | Bio parent does | Not yet), a quote with what to say to your partner about the ask, and a callout on the typical timeline for bonding with older kids.

tools.title: Discipline agreement
tools.subtitle: Same rules, agreed in private
tools.prompt: Flashpoints: {flashpoints}; enforcement now: {who_enforces}. Build a table (Rule | Applies to whom | Who enforces | Consequence), steps for the private partner meeting to agree it, a quote with how the bio parent introduces the rules to the kids (stepparent present but not presenting), and a callout on the 'monitor, don't discipline' principle for the first year.

tools.title: 'You're not my mum'
tools.subtitle: The line every stepparent hears

inputs.label: What the child said / did
inputs.placeholder: 'You can't tell me what to do, you're not my dad'

tools.prompt: The child ({age}) said: {said}. Give a quote with a calm in-the-moment reply (under 25 words, agrees with the true part, holds the house rule), text on what the child is really testing (2–3 sentences), bullets of 3 things not to say, and a checklist for the follow-up with your partner that evening.

tools.title: New-family rituals
tools.subtitle: Traditions that belong to this household

inputs.label: What the kids enjoy
inputs.placeholder: Mia loves baking, Tom gaming, Ella dinosaurs

tools.prompt: Suggest {freq} rituals for this blended family, kids' interests: {likes}. 5 cards (meta = minutes · cost · which kids), a quote with how to pitch the first one without making it a big deal, bullets on including the kids' other-household traditions respectfully, and a callout on what to do when a child refuses to join.

tools.title: Loyalty binds
tools.subtitle: Kids caught between two homes

inputs.label: What you're seeing
inputs.placeholder: Mia says she's not allowed to like me, goes quiet after weekends at her mum's

tools.prompt: Observed: {signs}. Text explaining loyalty binds in plain language (3 sentences), a quote with what the stepparent can say to the child to release the pressure, a second quote for the bio parent to say, a checklist of things never to say about the other household, and a callout on when a family therapist helps.

disclaimer: Family coaching only. Custody, consent and safeguarding matters should be checked with a family lawyer or child-welfare professional.
